claim: Girona Cathedral cultural visit ticket is €5 (students/65+ €3, under 7 free, audioguide included); open Apr-Oct 10:00-20:00 and Nov-Mar 10:00-19:00, with free Sunday entry to Treasury and Cloister
quote: Cultural visit €5 (includes audioguide); students/65+: €3; under 7: free. April-October: 10:00 to 20:00; November-March: 10:00 to 19:00. Free Sundays (Treasury & Cloister 10:00-14:00)

claim: Girona Cathedral has the widest Gothic nave in the world at 22.98 m, second-widest nave of any ecclesiastical style after St Peter's in Rome; the single Gothic nave was begun by Guillem Bofill and Antoni Canet in 1416
quote: a large Gothic nave—the widest Gothic nave in the world—at 22.98 m... surpassed only by St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Guillem Bofill and Antoni Canet started the project in 1416

claim: Girona Cathedral's Baroque main facade (begun 1606) sits atop ninety stone steps, with the staircase completed in 1607
quote: a Baroque facade at the top of ninety stone steps... The church has a Baroque main façade (begun in 1606)... preceded by a large staircase completed in 1607

claim: The Cathedral Treasury houses the Tapestry of Creation (Tapis de la Creació, c. 11th-12th century), a jewel of Catalan Romanesque art
quote: the Tapis de la Creació (Tapestry of the Creation, c. XI-XII), described as one of the jewels of Romanesque art in Catalonia

claim: Basilica of Sant Feliu opens Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00, Sun/holidays 13:00-18:00; combined Cathedral + Sant Feliu ticket is €7.50 (€5 reduced); it holds eight 4th-century pagan and early-Christian sarcophagi and a 14th-century Recumbent Christ by Aloi de Montbrai
quote: Cathedral + Basilica of Sant Feliu: €7.50 / €5.00 / €1.50... eight pagan and early Christian sarcophagi (4th century)... Recumbent Christ (14th century) by the sculptor Aloi de Montbrai... Mon to Sat 10AM-6PM; Sundays and bank holidays 1PM-6PM

claim: Museum of Jewish History admission is €6 (€3 reduced; under 16 free; free first Sunday of each month); open Sep-Jun Tue-Sat 10:00-18:00, Mon/Sun/holidays 10:00-14:00, with extended summer hours in Jul-Aug
quote: General Admission: €6. Reduced Rate: €3... Free Entry: Children under 16... Free admission on the first Sunday of every month. September to June: Tuesday to Saturday from 10 am to 6 pm; Monday, Sunday and bank holidays from 10 am to 2 pm

claim: The Museum of Jewish History occupies the former Call within El Call and uses eleven thematic galleries to cover medieval Catalan Jewish life, including the aljama, synagogues, cemeteries and the Inquisition
quote: eleven galleries organized around thematic areas covering medieval Jewish life in Catalonia... The main aim of the Museum is to preserve and reflect the history of the Jewish communities of Catalonia

claim: Girona's Call was one of the most important Jewish communities in the medieval West and is the best-preserved Jewish quarter in Europe, home to the community for some six centuries
quote: one of the most important Jewish communities in the West and is currently the best preserved call in Europe. The Jewish community lived here 6 centuries

claim: Girona's Arab Baths charge €3 general admission (€2 over-65, €1 students/under-16/unemployed) and open Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00, Sun/holidays 10:00-14:00
quote: General Admission Price: 3 euros per person. Reduced Price: 2 euros per person for those over 65... 1 euro per person... Monday through Saturday: 10 am to 6 pm; Sundays and bank holidays: 10 am to 2 pm

claim: Girona's Arab Baths are a 12th-century Romanesque bathhouse modelled on Roman and Moorish baths despite the name
quote: Arab Baths of Girona... Romanesque

claim: Sant Pere de Galligants is a Romanesque monastery (begun late 10th century, completed 12th century) now housing the Girona branch of the Archaeology Museum of Catalonia
quote: located in the Sant Pere de Galligants Monastery in the historic centre of the city... a Romanesque religious building whose construction began at the end of the 10th century and was completed in the 12th century

claim: Girona's medieval city walls (Passeig de la Muralla) are freely walkable along the old town, offering elevated views over the city and cathedral
quote: The Walls | Tourism | Girona City Council

claim: Girona stood in for Braavos, King's Landing and Oldtown in Game of Thrones Season 6: the Cathedral steps were the Great Sept of Baelor (Jaime vs the High Sparrow), the Jewish Quarter and Sant Martí Sacosta steps were Braavos (Arya/the Waif), Sant Pere de Galligants was Oldtown's Citadel, and the Arab Baths and a nearby bridge featured in Arya's chase
quote: Cathedral Steps: exterior for the Great Sept of Baelor... Jewish Quarter Streets depicted the city of Braavos where Arya Stark's storyline unfolded... Sant Pere de Galligants Monastery represented the citadel in Oldtown... Arab Baths used as a location where Arya is trying to hide while fleeing from the waif. All locations filmed during Season 6

claim: The Pont de les Peixateries Velles (Eiffel Bridge) was designed by Gustave Eiffel's company and completed in 1877, just before the Eiffel Tower; it is a bright red iron lattice bridge.
quote: Completed in 1877 ... designed by Gustave Eiffel's company just before he built the Eiffel Tower ... Bright red iron structure ... a striking contrast to the colorful riverside houses

claim: The Eiffel Bridge offers arguably the best view of Girona's cathedral and the Cases de l'Onyar, while Pont de Pedra gives views over the Cathedral and coloured houses; sunrise is the ideal shooting time.
quote: maybe the best view of Girona's cathedral and the Cases de l'Onyar ... Pont de Pedra ... views over the Cathedral and the famous coloured houses by the river ... wake up early, and you will have it all for yourself

claim: The Passeig de la Muralla wall walk is completely free, takes about 1-2 hours, with access points near the Cathedral, Jardins dels Alemanys and Plaça Catalunya; Torre Gironella is the highest point with 360-degree views toward the Pyrenees.
quote: completely free to visit ... access points near the Girona Cathedral, Jardins dels Alemanys, and Plaça Catalunya ... Torre Gironella ... the highest point on the Girona City Walls ... 360-degree views

claim: The colourful houses are locally called Cases de l'Onyar; they were restored in 1983-1984 by the Fuses-Viader studio in a warm-colour palette, and golden hour before sunset gives the most vibrant reflections.
quote: locally known as 'Cases de l'Onyar' ... restoration of Cases de l'Onyar was made in 1983-1984 by the architect studio Fuses-Viader, following a warm-colored palette ... golden hour just before sunset

claim: The best way from Girona to Figueres is by train (Rodalies de Catalunya), running hourly and taking about 30 minutes; AVANT high-speed trains do it in ~15 minutes.
quote: The best way to get from Girona to Figueres is by train, which takes 30 minutes. Rodalies de Catalunya operates trains from Girona to Figueres hourly, with tickets costing $6-15.

claim: Dalí Theatre-Museum general admission is €18.50 online / €20.50 at the desk; reduced €15.00 online; under-8s free; it holds the world's most extensive Dalí collection (1,500+ pieces).
quote: General admission: €18.50 (online) or €20.50 (at ticket desk)... houses the world's most extensive collection of Dalí's work with over 1,500 pieces.

claim: The Dalí Theatre-Museum opened 28 September 1974, displays the single largest collection of Dalí's work, received 1,368,755 visitors in 2016, and Dalí is buried in a crypt below the stage.
quote: The museum opened on September 28, 1974... received 1,368,755 visitors in 2016... displays the single largest and most diverse collection of works by Salvador Dalí.

claim: The Dalí Museum is among the most-visited museums in Spain, drawing over a million visitors a year, with its Figueres ranking placing it second/third nationally behind the Prado and Reina Sofía.
quote: The Dalí Museum in Figueres, founded in 1974, is one of the most visited museums in Spain. It draws over a million visitors a year and holds the world's largest collection of the artist's work.

claim: Besalú has no train station; a Teisa/TEISA bus from Girona runs roughly every 2 hours and takes about 50 minutes, otherwise reach it by car.
quote: Transports Elèctrics Interurbans S.A. operates a bus from Girona to Besalú every 2 hours... the journey taking 50 minutes. Besalú is not on a train line so you'll need to take a bus.

claim: Besalú lies about 30 km from Girona (roughly a 30-40 minute drive) and is famed for its 12th-century Romanesque bridge of seven arches and two towers guarding the old town, plus preserved Jewish heritage.
quote: Besalú is located in the comarca of Garrotxa, some 30 kilometers from the city of Girona... The large, well-preserved Romanesque bridge is supported by seven arcs and two towers, and gracefully guards the entrance to the old town.

claim: From Girona, Costa Brava resorts are reachable by Teisa/Sarfa/Sagalés bus: Sant Feliu de Guíxols ~30 min car / 50 min bus, Tossa de Mar ~40 min car / 1 hr bus, Cadaqués ~1.5 hr car / 2 hr bus.
quote: Sant Feliu de Guíxols: 30 minutes by car, 50 minutes by bus; Tossa de Mar: 40 minutes by car, 1 hour by bus... Cadaqués: 1.5 hours by car, 2 hours by bus. Main operators include Teisa, Sarfa, and Sagalés.

claim: Direct buses from Girona to Cadaqués (Moventis Sarfa) are the cheapest option but run only once daily with none on weekends, taking ~1h45-2h; line 33 connects Cadaqués town to Cap de Creus.
quote: Buses going directly from Girona to Cadaqués are the most affordable option, but they run once daily (none on weekends) and will take 1 hour and 45 minutes... there is a line 33 from Ajuntament de Cadaqués to Cap de Creus.

claim: The Camí de Ronda coastal path links Costa Brava towns and coves including Calella de Palafrugell, Begur, Palamós and Sant Feliu de Guíxols; the linear Sant Feliu-to-Begur route is 43 km, with an 18 km Palamós-to-Tamariu weekend stage.
quote: Lineal Route (St. Feliu de Guíxols to Begur): 43 kilometers... Weekend option: Palamos to Tamariu (18 km)... The path links numerous coastal locations, including Calella de Palafrugell, Palamós, Platja d'Aro, Begur, Sant Feliu de Guíxols.

claim: Sarfa/Moventis bus line 41 connects Girona to Palafrugell (gateway to Calella de Palafrugell), with the trip taking roughly 60 minutes.
quote: Bus service 41 connects Palafrugell to Girona, with the total trip duration approximately 60 minutes.

claim: The Dalí Theatre-Museum (~1.1 million visitors in 2018) outdraws Barcelona's Picasso Museum (~948,000) and ranks among the world's 50 most-visited museums, though teamLab Borderless surpassed it as the top single-artist museum globally.
quote: In 2018, teamLab Borderless and teamLab Planets welcomed more visitors than the Picasso Museum in Barcelona (948,483 visitors) and the Dalí Theatre-Museum in Figueres (1,105,169 visitors). However, it is one of the 50 most visited museums in the world.

claim: The xuixo is a deep-fried, sugar-coated cylindrical pastry filled with crema catalana that originated in 1920s Girona at Emili Puig's shop on Carrer Cort Reial.
quote: It is assumed that this viennoiserie originated in 1920s Girona in a shop owned by Emili Puig in the Street Cort Reial. ... It is a deep-fried, sugar-coated cylindrical product filled with crema catalana.

claim: Local legend credits the xuixo's name to el Tarlà, an acrobat who sneezed (xui-xui) while courting a pastry chef's daughter and promised the pastry's recipe.
quote: the invention of the Xuixo has to be credited to el Tarlà ... He sneezed (which sounds like xui-xui) and was discovered ... He named it after the sneeze that betrayed him.

claim: Mercat del Lleó is Girona's municipal market operating since 1944 at Plaça Calvet i Rubalcaba 15, with over 50 stalls and 150 professionals selling fresh meat, fish, charcuterie, produce, prepared dishes and wines, plus a bar for breakfast.
quote: El Mercat del Lleó és el mercat municipal de Girona. ... Des de 1944 ... més de 50 parades i 150 professionals ... un bar a on esmorzar-hi. ... Plaça Calvet i Rubalcaba, 15, 17002 – Girona

claim: Rocambolesc's flagship gelateria is at Carrer Santa Clara 50, 17001 Girona, selling soft ice cream plus chocolates, candies and confectionery, with a separate Bikineria at C/ de les Hortes 6.
quote: Gelateria: Carrer Sta. Clara 50, 17001 Girona ... soft ice cream, polo shirts, jars, and many other sweet preparations ... Bikineria: C/ de les Hortes número 6, 17001 Girona

claim: Rocambolesc is run by pastry chef Jordi Roca, the youngest of the Roca brothers behind El Celler de Can Roca, who uses the restaurant's dessert team to develop its gelato.
quote: Jordi Roca, the youngest brother and pastry chef, runs the ice cream shop's ... locations when he's not working at El Celler de Can Roca. ... Jordi utilizes the restaurant's dessert team to create rich, smooth, flavorful soft serve ice cream

claim: Empordà is the wine DO covering the northeast corner of Catalonia in Girona province, split into Alt Empordà and Baix Empordà subzones, with reds made mainly from Carinyena and Garnatxa and whites from Macabeu.
quote: Empordà is a Spanish Denominación de Origen Protegida ... in the province of Girona ... divided into two subzones: the northern Alt Empordà ... and the southern Baix Empordà ... red wines ... primarily made with the Carinyena and Garnatxa varieties

claim: Girona's best tapas include Basque-style pintxos venues such as Txalaka and Zanpanzar, with bars clustering around Plaça de la Independència and the Rambla de la Llibertat in the old town.
quote: Txalaka offers a trip to the Basque Country with an almost infinite variety of tapas and pintxos served on small slices of bread ... Zanpanzar offers authentic Basque cuisine with an impressive array of pintxos served on crusty bread

claim: Girona's Barri Vell old town has a dense bar scene including Sunset Jazz Club (speakeasy-style cocktails) and Vermuteria Lola for local vermouth and tapas.
quote: Sunset Jazz Club ... cosy, speakeasy-style joint ... impressive selection of spirits and cocktails. ... Vermuteria Lola ... where local vermouth and tapas come together ... The narrow, winding streets of the historic Barri Vell ... are brimming with bars

claim: Plaça de la Independència is a lively neoclassical arcaded square surrounded by tapas bars and restaurants, a central dining spot in Girona.
quote: Placa de la Independencia features a lively environment with good tapas bars and restaurants that surround the courtyard.

claim: Around 300 professional cyclists, triathletes, sports directors, mechanics and physios live in Girona, with pro teams including Cannondale-Garmin, EF-Drapac, Mitchelton-Scott and Israel Cycling Academy based there.
quote: About 300 professional cyclists, triathletes, sports directors, mechanics and physiotherapists live here ... professional teams are based here: Cannondale-Garmin, today Education First-Drapac, Mitchelton-Scott, Israel Cycling Academy

claim: Girona is established as a cycling capital with around 100 pro riders living there at least part of the year; signature climbs include Rocacorba (the Girona classic) and Els Angels, plus the Banyoles lake loop.
quote: Girona is now well established as a capital of cycling ... Rocacorba ... the Girona classic ... famous (or infamous)

claim: Eat Sleep Cycle's Girona hub combines a bike shop, workshop, apparel store, bike-hire centre, cafe and terrace in the city centre and refreshes its rental fleet annually from leading brands.
quote: Eat Sleep Cycle offers a bike shop, workshop, apparel store, bike hire centre, café and sunny terrace in the centre of Girona.

claim: The 2026 Girona bike-hire fleet features newly released models including the Colnago Y1Rs, with the aim of giving renters a brand-new-bike feeling.
quote: The 2026 Girona bike rental fleet features newly released models ... the Colnago Y1Rs, which is available for rental in Girona in 2026 and is expected to be fully booked.

claim: The Carrilet I greenway runs 58 km from Olot (440 m) down to Girona (70 m) along an old narrow-gauge railway through the Garrotxa Volcanic Area and Ter valley, suitable for cyclists and hikers.
quote: The Carrilet I greenway descends smoothly from Olot (440 m) to Girona (70 m) ... It begins in the Garrotxa Volcanic Area, and following the old narrow-gauge railway line, reaches the Ter valley

claim: The Carrilet II greenway stretches about 42 km on a gentle incline from Girona to the coast at Sant Feliu de Guixols, following the former Girona-beach rail line and passing old stations converted to cyclist-friendly bars.
quote: The Carrilet II greenway stretches out 41.9 km. With a smooth incline from Girona to Sant Feliu de Guíxols (15 m), its highest point is in the municipality of Llagostera (149 m)

claim: The Olot-Girona Carrilet route, with around 1.5 million users a year, is the most popular via verde (greenway) in Spain.
quote: With 1.5 million users a year, this is the most popular via verde (greenway) in Spain.

claim: The Lake Banyoles loop is a flat, easy circular trail of about 6.9 km (roughly 1h45) with continuous lake views and traditional fishing huts, walkable or cyclable for all ages.
quote: the Tour around Lake Banyoles, a 4.3-mile (6.9 km) trail that takes 1 hour 46 minutes to complete with easy, circular paths offering continuous views of the lake and passing traditional fishing huts

claim: Day-trip hikes near Girona include the La Garrotxa volcanic park circuit of Santa Margarida and Croscat volcanoes, a ~12 km loop of about 3h24.
quote: the Volcán de Santa Margarida and Volcán del Croscat - Circular through the Natural Park of the Volcanic Zone of La Garrotxa, a 7.5-mile (12.1 km) trail that takes 3 hours 24 minutes

claim: Guided sea-cave kayaking and snorkelling tours on the Costa Brava explore coves, caves and cliffs around the Bay of Sant Pol-S'Agaro, with equipment and lifejackets provided.
quote: kayak and snorkel in coves, caves, channels, exploring the cliffs and islands of the Bay of Sant Pol-S'Agaró

claim: Costa Brava kayak-and-snorkel tours near Girona run from spots like Blanes (from ~$47, 1.5h) and L'Estartit to the protected Medes Islands (from ~$34, 2.5h).
quote: tours in Blanes (starting from $47 for 1.5 hours) and from L'Estartit to the Medes Islands (from $34 for 2.5 hours)

claim: Globus Emporda has run hot-air balloon flights over the Emporda for more than 20 years, departing early morning from Colomers (~30 min from Girona) for roughly an hour aloft over fields and villages.
quote: More than 20 years flying in the Empordà ... Approximately one hour floating silently over fields and villages ... Parc del Ter s/n, 17144 Colomers, Girona

claim: Barcelona Sants to Girona high-speed trains run ~30/day, fastest ~38 min, average ~1 hour, on AVE/Avant/Euromed, with fares from roughly $9 when booked in advance.
quote: The route's fastest journey takes 38 minutes... There are around 30 trains per day... Train tickets from Barcelona to Girona start from as little as $8.92... You can travel from Barcelona to Girona on AVE, Renfe, Avant and Euromed trains.

claim: Girona's Temps de Flors 2026 runs May 9-17, daily 9:30am-9pm, free admission, with floral installations in monuments, courtyards and gardens across the old town.
quote: FROM MAY 9 TO 17 2026... Every day from 9.30 am. to 9 pm... Free... Embellishment and floral art installations in monuments, courtyards and gardens around the city.

claim: Girona-Costa Brava airport (GRO) sits ~18km from the city; bus 607 runs hourly to the centre in ~20-25 min, and a Barcelona Bus links the airport to Barcelona Estacio del Nord in ~1h10.
quote: Bus number 607 running hourly between 4:00am and midnight... travel from the city center to the airport in 20 to 25 minutes... the Barcelona Bus service leaves Girona airport for Barcelona Estació del Nord with a journey time of 1 hour and 10 minutes.

claim: Two to three days is ideal for a Girona weekend; the compact historic core can be toured in 4-5 hours, and a third day suits day trips to Figueres or Besalu.
quote: A weekend (two to three days) in Girona will provide you with more time... you can easily tour the city... in as little as 4 or 5 hours... If you have three days, spend your final day on a day trip... Figueres and Besalú are great options.

claim: Girona is small and walkable; it is best not to bring a car into town, and everything is reachable on foot with 10 local bus routes as backup.
quote: Girona is a walkable city and easy to explore on foot... it's best not to bring a car into town... The town is small enough that you can likely walk anywhere you want to go, but if you need transit, there are 10 local bus routes.

claim: Barri Vell (Old Town) is the best base for first-timers, putting the Cathedral and Jewish Quarter within walking distance, with Eixample across the river as a cheaper alternative and Mercadal good for families.
quote: staying in Barri Vell makes the most sense as it puts you right in the middle of the main sights... Eixample is a great option and it's just across the river from the old town... Mercadal is a great option where you're within easy reach of the main sights.

claim: Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) are the best times to visit Girona, around 20-22C, while July-August regularly hit 30-33C with peak crowds.
quote: Spring (April-May) and Autumn (September-October) are widely recommended as the ideal periods... temperatures in July and August regularly reach 30-33°C... The best times to visit Girona are from mid-May to mid-June and from mid-September to mid-October.
